title: Each event once across loads
prompt: The tracking feed sometimes delivers an event twice, on the same day or a day later. `process()` already appends each new load to bronze. Finish it so silver gets one row per event, adding only the events it doesn't have yet.
rules: Silver has one row per `event_id`, with the columns in `EVENT_COLUMNS` (no `load_date`). A repeated delivery is the same event, whether it comes in the same load or a later one.
Every landed event is in silver, however often `process()` runs.
Each run adds to silver; it doesn't rebuild it from bronze.
hints: Without `load_date`, two deliveries of one event are the same row: `select(EVENT_COLUMNS).distinct()` keeps one.
An event can already be in silver from an earlier run. Collect silver's `event_id` values into a list and drop the new events whose id is in it, with `~F.col("event_id").isin(...)`.
On the first run there's no silver table yet: check with `DeltaTable.isDeltaTable`.
starter:
import shutil

from pyspark.sql import functions as F
from delta.tables import DeltaTable

LANDING = "/tmp/landing/shipment_events"
BRONZE = "/tmp/bronze/shipment_events"
SILVER = "/tmp/silver/events"
EVENT_COLUMNS = ["event_id", "shipment_id", "warehouse_id", "event_type", "event_time", "location", "sequence"]


def deliver(shipment_events, days):
    # These load days land in the landing folder, one folder per day. Don't change this.
    (shipment_events.filter(F.col("load_date").isin(days))
        .write.mode("append").partitionBy("load_date").parquet(LANDING))


def process():
    # 1. Bronze: append the landed rows after bronze's high-water mark, as they arrived.
    if DeltaTable.isDeltaTable(spark, BRONZE):
        mark = spark.read.format("delta").load(BRONZE).select(F.max("load_date")).first()[0]
    else:
        mark = None
    landing = spark.read.parquet(LANDING)
    new = landing if mark is None else landing.filter(F.col("load_date") > mark)
    new.write.format("delta").mode("append").save(BRONZE)

    # 2. Silver: one row per event; add only events it doesn't have yet.
    pass

def solve(shipment_events):
    shutil.rmtree("/tmp/landing", ignore_errors=True)  # start from empty folders on every run
    shutil.rmtree("/tmp/bronze", ignore_errors=True)
    shutil.rmtree("/tmp/silver", ignore_errors=True)
    days = sorted(r.load_date for r in shipment_events.select("load_date").distinct().collect())
    deliver(shipment_events, days[:1])
    process()
    deliver(shipment_events, days[1:])
    process()
    process()  # a rerun: nothing new has landed
    return spark.read.format("delta").load(SILVER)
explanation: Bronze keeps every delivery with its `load_date`; silver keeps the event. Repeats come in two ways. In one load, `new.select(EVENT_COLUMNS).distinct()` folds copies together, because without `load_date` they are the same row, even when the copy landed a day later in the same delivery. Across loads, the copy of E0000007 lands on 4 March, after the first run has already put the event in silver, so the run also drops the events whose `event_id` silver already has: collect those ids and filter with `~F.col("event_id").isin(seen)`. On the rerun there's nothing new, so the append is empty. `distinct()` with `load_date` still in the rows keeps a copy that landed a day later, and overwriting silver with each load loses the earlier runs.
